subject: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint

Team,

Attached is the monthly_kpi_dashboard_v2.csv (export from the dashboard) and a short high-level readout: latency per-model, cost/token breakdown, uptime incidents, and usage segmentation. For QBR next week we need a clean narrative and 1-slide per major signal:

- Latency: model-x p50 has regressed from 120ms -> 210ms over the last two weeks; p95 shows intermittent spikes.
- Cost: embeddings spend +18% MoM; influenced by a small set of high-embedding-volume tenants.
- Uptime: single 12m incident on 2028-07-14 tied to autoscaling flaps in eu-west-1; follow-up ticket created (INF-4892).
- Usage: spike from partner pilot (AeroFin) — we should confirm quota and contract expectations.

Asks:
1) Please call out owners and a short remediation or mitigation plan for each signal by EOD 2028-07-24.
2) If any metric requires an OKR adjustment (target or stretch), flag it in your reply.
3) I want a 30-minute sync the week of 7/25 to finalize the QBR one-pager and owner slides — propose times.

Irene — will need a short root-cause note for latency (high level) so I can include an exec summary.
Laura — please confirm whether we should move Cost/unit OKR to an interim target.
Markus — any reliability mitigations you recommend short-term?

Thanks,
David
David Kim
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: monthly_kpi_dashboard_v2.csv (CSV, 220KB)
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_kpi_qbr
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint

Thanks David — quick notes below (attaching latency_rootcause_notes.pdf):

- Preliminary root cause: backpressure due to a small set of long-request streams holding KV caches open and preventing efficient batching. We saw queue growth coincident with the AeroFin pilot peak (7/12–7/15).
- Short-term mitigation (next 48–72h): apply a conservative KV-cache TTL for long-run workers and introduce an inter-request preempt flag for streams >60s to force earlier flush. Expected p50 improvement ~30–40ms across model-x.
- Medium: rollout of a dynamic batching policy that de-prioritizes long-running streams during bursts — target rollout 7/31 (can be canaryed).

Action owners:
- Irene: implement TTL change + monitor (INF-4901)
- Platform: Markus to schedule canary for dynamic batching and confirm rollback plan
- Analytics: Laura to validate dashboard filters and confirm AeroFin's usage breakdown

Will share a 1-page RCA and expected impact numbers by 7/24.

Irene Choi
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency_rootcause_notes.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint

Adding analytics context — pulled a few slices from the dashboard and updated the shared spreadsheet (link below).

Key points:
- AeroFin accounts for ~24% of the embeddings spend increase; 3 tenant IDs are responsible for ~80% of that spike.
- Model-x latency spikes correlate with a specific workload class (batch inference for long sequences). p95 is influenced by extreme outliers (tail requests).
- Uptime incident — the autoscaling policy behaved within config but hit a cross-region quota; cloud provider throttled scale-up briefly. We have requested quota bump for eu-west-1 and filed a follow-up with the provider.

Recommendation on OKR: move Cost/unit from target=0.08 -> interim target=0.085 for Q3, but add a parallel initiative metric to reduce the high-consuming tenants (owner: Product Growth).

I've updated the Drive folder with a chart (latency_model_x_7day.png) and the sheet: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_kpi_qbr

Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Analytics
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint

Echoing Irene & Laura — quick operational commits: 

- Canary rollout: dynamic batching (de-prioritize long streams) scheduled 7/31 -> canary window 7/31–8/02 in us-west-2 with 10% traffic. Rollback plan in INF-4910.
- Immediate: will apply the KV-cache TTL change tomorrow AM (owner: platform infra). Expect a p50 shift ~35ms based on sim.
- Reliability guardrails: adding a temporary quota cap for new partner tenants (AeroFin pilot) to avoid noisy neighbor risk while we tune endpoints.

I'll update the dashboard with a 'canary' slice and create the exec slide for the reliability item.

Markus Klein
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform KPI triage — QBR readiness & OKR checkpoint

Thanks for the rapid responses and clear owners — finalizing the action tracker and next steps for the QBR readout. Consolidated asks below (I'll include this in the exec deck draft):

Action tracker (owners & due dates):
- Irene: one-page RCA with expected impact numbers, attach to exec deck (due 2028-07-31) — ticket INF-4901.
- Markus: canary rollout plan + rollback runbook (due 2028-07-30) — ticket INF-4910.
- Laura: updated cost breakdown and a proposed OKR language change for Cost/unit (due 2028-07-31).
- Soojin: assemble the one-slide per-signal readouts into qbr_readout_draft.pptx and share by 2028-08-02.

Decisions:
- We will temporarily cap partner tenant concurrency until canary completes.
- OKR: move to interim Cost/unit=0.085 for next Q, capture initiative to reduce heavy tenants as a separate OKR.

Next steps: please drop final artifacts into the Drive folder and mark them in the sheet. I've created a short calendar block for 7/31 10:00–10:30 to run through the slides (invite sent). If anyone cannot make it, ping me and I'll record a short readout.

I'll include INF-4892, INF-4901, INF-4910 in the QBR appendix as follow-ups.

Thanks — solid progress.

David
David Kim
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
